newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Diplomat says Kabila on way to Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Diplomat says Kabila on way to Zaire talks.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila left Luanda on Saturday apparently to join an international peace summit on board a South African navy ship where President Mobutu Sese Seko is awaiting their first face-to-face talks, witnesses said.

"We believe Kabila has left Luanda and is on his way to meet Mobutu," a senior Western diplomat in Angola told Reuters. Witnesses said Kabila's plane, bearing a Ugandan flag, departed at 9.40 a.m. (0840 GMT).

Kabila had arrived in the Angolan capital on Friday from the rebel stronghold of Lubumbashi in southeast Zaire in readiness to travel with South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki to the talks in international waters off the coast of West Africa.
But the rebel leader pulled out of the arrangements late on Friday, demanding guarantees of his security and a say in the composition of the summit.

Mbeki, who left the Angolan capital to discuss Kabila's concerns with talks chairman President Nelson Mandela earlier on Friday evening, had been due to return to Luanda on Saturday to brief Kabila about security measures on the ship.
South African officials said he was still on board the ship on Saturday morning, without giving further details.
At his Luanda press conference, Kabila committed himself to finding a peaceful solution for Zaire.
"If we wanted to we could win this militarily in two weeks...(But) suggestions that I am stalling for time are ridiculous. I am interested in finding a peaceful solution to the problem," he said.

Kabila has led a seven-month-old rebellion against Mobutu's 32-year rule and his troops are gathering near the capital Kinshasa. The rebels are now estimated to have control of three-quarters of the country.
The president's aides have said Mobutu wants to discuss a transition period ahead of elections but Kabila has insisted he is ready only to discuss Mobutu's immediate departure from power.
Aged 66 and suffering from prostate cancer, Mobutu is one of Africa's most enduring strongmen, backed during the Cold War by the United States as a bulwark against Soviet communism.
